thread:
sam: Customer repro: invoke to analytics.create keeps failing with a JSON schema validation error. Customer sent a small batch, gateway returns 400. Error: \"additionalProperties not allowed: \u2018meta\u2019\". Happening on hosted/redwood-us-east.

ivy: Can you paste the raw request body and the exact error snippet?

sam: Pasting the request we got from the customer (sanitized):
```json
{\n  \"model\": \"open-llm/analytics-annotator-v1\",\n  \"tool\": \"analytics.create\",\n  \"tool_args\": {\n    \"events\": [ { \"type\": \"click\", \"target\": \"btn-buy\" } ],\n    \"context\": { \"customerId\": \"cust_123\" }\n  },\n  \"meta\": { \"env\": \"staging\" }\n}\n```

sam: Gateway logs show: 
```
ValidationError: request.body: additionalProperties \u2018meta\u2019 is not allowed
 at validate (/srv/gateway/node_modules/ajv/dist/ajv.js:...)
 at middleware (/srv/gateway/src/validate.js:45)
```

kate: Two things to note: 1) API expects `context.customer_id` (snake_case) not `customerId` — that will make the required field check fail, but it wouldn't trigger additionalProperties. 2) We disallow top-level extra keys (additionalProperties: false) so `meta` is rejected.

ivy: Interesting — customer added `meta` as a top-level convenience. We used to accept misc top-level metadata but tightened the schema in 2025-11 to prevent routing ambiguity. Could be a churn-related breaking change.

sam: Repro steps I ran locally (failing):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/invoke -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '@payload.json' # payload.json contains the JSON above
```
Response: 400 + body: `{\"error\":\"request.body: additionalProperties 'meta' is not allowed\"}`

ivy: Minimal repro: drop `meta` and rename `customerId` -> `customer_id` and it passes validation. But we should decide: do we (a) relax top-level additionalProperties to true and move strictness into named fields, (b) accept a top-level `meta` bag only if it is object with freeform allowed, or (c) keep strict and document the breaking change?

kate: Leaning toward option (b) — allow a single optional `metadata` object with additionalProperties=true. That keeps routing keys strict while giving customers a safe place. But we need to check downstream services — analytics.create handler expects no `meta` at top-level.

eng-platform-oncall: FYI I'm going to tag this as P2 customer escal. @kate can you add a short RFC and impact matrix? I'll create an incident ticket for the customer escalation so CS has tracking.

sam: Creating a small PR branch to shim incoming requests in the gateway that maps `customerId` -> `customer_id` and relocates unknown top-level keys into `metadata` (temp fix). Posting PR link when ready.

support-bot: Escalation created: ESCL-2026-482, linked to ticket #4321. Assigned to eng-platform. :white_check_mark:

ivy: Also leaving a note for SDK team: client libs should normalize casing and avoid top-level custom keys. We should push a patch to the Node SDK that warns when unknown top-level props are present.

sam: Put the customer repro + curl + raw payload in ticket #4321. They'll test a patched gateway tomorrow morning and confirm.

kate: Thanks — I'll start the RFC draft and list the compatibility options. If we go with (b) we'll need a short migration doc, a test plan (schema unit tests + e2e with analytics handler), and a rollout canary.

eng-platform-oncall: Noted. Closing loop: assign to eng-platform team and keep CS updated.
